title: Binary Tree Right Side View
statement_short: Given the root of a binary tree, imagine yourself standing on the right side of it, return the values of the nodes you can see ordered from top to bottom.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in tree <= 100, -100 <= Node.val <= 100
hint: Small node count (<= 100) allows level-order traversal, capturing the last element of each queue level.
why_not: Right: Tree BFS traverses level by level, picking the last node in each level queue in O(n) time and O(w) space. Not Tree DFS: Pre-order (root-right-left) DFS works by tracking depth, but level-order BFS directly groups nodes by level. Not Two Pointers: Scanning pointer pairs cannot navigate hierarchical level structures natively. Not 1D DP: Subproblem state memoization does not apply to spatial tree view projections.
